It is a box which allows those within it to travel backwards and forwards through time and space, as interpreted by an external observer. Timelike observers travel within the interior of a \u2018bubble\u2019 of geometry which moves along a circular, acausal trajectory through spacetime. If certain timelike observers inside the bubble maintain a persistent acceleration, their worldlines will close.<\/jats:p>\n                  <jats:p>Our analysis includes a description of the causal structure of our spacetime, as well as a discussion of its physicality. The inclusion of such a bubble in a spacetime will render the background spacetime non-orientable, generating additional consistency constraints for formulations of the initial value problem. BV","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"<jats:p>The stability of Traversable Wormhole solutions traditionally requires the violation of the Null Energy Condition (NEC) by \"exotic matter.\" In this work, we demonstrate that such violation is an artifact of neglecting the distributional structure of singular spacetime boundaries. Utilizing the Gelfand-Leray Double Layer formalism, we perform a detailed, step-by-step derivation of the tangential pressure S \u03b8\u03b8 at the throat of a Morris-Thorne wormhole. We prove that the required \"exotic\" stress is exactly provided by the jump in extrinsic curvature induced by the Double Layer. Furthermore, we define the effective potential V ef f (R) of the throat dynamics and prove that the topological stiffness of the vacuum (governed by the Dilaton coupling \u03be \u2265 1) guarantees radial stability against perturbations. This identifies the \"exotic matter\" not as a bulk substance, but as the elastic response of the Amplitude Geometry to the violation of the fundamental tubular thickness.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.6169855","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,3,10]],"date-time":"2026-03-10T09:45:11Z","timestamp":1773135911000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Double
